globalInvariants: Android 15 only: minSdk 35 and targetSdk 35; sideloaded APK, no Play Store work.
app/src/main/assets/schedule.json is the only production source of timetable/task definitions. No weekday/time/task literals may be duplicated in Kotlin for production behavior.
Repository-root AUDIOS/ and VISUAL/ are authoritative user materials and must not be renamed, edited or replaced by agents.
Weekends contain no alarms. Missed alarms are skipped permanently and never replayed after boot/app restart.
Only the next future alert is scheduled; each delivered alert fires once.
Audio rotation is persistent deterministic round-robin 1.mp3→2.mp3→3.mp3→1.mp3 and advances only when real playback starts.
Alarm playback uses Android alarm audio usage/system alarm volume. The app must never raise, lock or override the user's system volume.
Alarm UI has no in-app dismiss/snooze action and closes automatically when audio completes; OS-level controls remain under Android/user control.
Full-screen intent is used only for actual alarm delivery. Normal app UI is schedule/current/next plus setup-required actions when capabilities are missing.
12:00 uses IRSE.png for the alert while the normal display state becomes ESCUELA.
No network, account, analytics, cloud, remote configuration, schedule editor or background polling is in scope.
All task agents must leave laya/** untouched; the package/oracles are external acceptance material.

items.title: Scaffold Android 15 application
items.objective: Create the buildable Android 15-only GERMAN FATHER app skeleton and deterministic Gradle/test baseline without moving or renaming the existing AUDIOS/ and VISUAL/ source materials.
acceptance: Repository contains a single Android application module that builds with minSdk 35 and targetSdk 35; compileSdk is at least 35.
Application id and namespace are com.pixatrip1984.germanfather.
A Gradle wrapper and pinned compatible Android/Kotlin toolchain are committed; the project builds using JDK 17.
Existing root AUDIOS/ and VISUAL/ files are preserved byte-for-byte and are not renamed or duplicated as hand-maintained copies.
A baseline JVM unit test runs through :app:testDebugUnitTest and a debug APK can be assembled.
validation: Run the authoritative Gradle unit-test, lint, and debug-APK gates.
Inspect the Android configuration for API 35 minimum/target and the expected application id.
items.taskPrompt: Build the initial Android project for GERMAN FATHER. This is an Android 15-only sideloaded alarm application; do not implement the alarm behavior yet. Use Kotlin and Jetpack Compose with a stable pinned Android Gradle Plugin/Gradle/Kotlin toolchain compatible with JDK 17 and API 35. Create one app module with namespace/applicationId com.pixatrip1984.germanfather, minSdk 35, targetSdk 35, and compileSdk >=35. Commit the Gradle wrapper. Keep the existing root AUDIOS/ and VISUAL/ directories unchanged: they are authoritative user-supplied media and later tasks will package them as assets. Create a minimal MainActivity/Compose shell only as needed to build. Establish test dependencies and at least one trivial JVM unit test so :app:testDebugUnitTest is a real gate. Do not add schedule logic, alarm scheduling, playback, permission flows, or a schedule editor in this task. Produce a deterministic build and document any toolchain assumption in README.md.

items.title: Add declarative schedule engine
items.objective: Make one schedule.json the only timetable/task definition and implement pure current/next/next-alert computation with the exact approved weekday schedule.
acceptance: app/src/main/assets/schedule.json matches the approved V1 schedule exactly and contains the persistent audio rotation order 1.mp3, 2.mp3, 3.mp3.
Monday/Wednesday/Friday and Tuesday/Thursday differ only where approved; Saturday and Sunday have no timeline events and no alerts.
At 12:00 the display timeline becomes ESCUELA while the alert at the same time is IRSE using IRSE.png.
The schedule parser validates duplicate times, malformed times, unknown days, missing task ids, missing visual references for alerts, and missing audio files.
Schedule calculations use the device local time zone, skip every alert whose scheduled wall-clock time is already in the past, and calculate the next future alert across day/week boundaries.
Changing timetable/task data does not require changing Kotlin code: production timetable literals do not exist outside schedule.json.
Root AUDIOS/ and VISUAL/ are packaged into the APK as Android assets without creating second hand-maintained copies.
validation: Run ScheduleRepositoryTest and ScheduleEngineTest with fixed clocks and week-boundary cases.
Run the external package schedule oracle against app/src/main/assets/schedule.json.
Build the APK so asset packaging is exercised.
items.taskPrompt: Implement the data boundary for the product. app/src/main/assets/schedule.json must be the single editable source of truth for timetable/task data. Use the exact approved schedule from the package oracle laya/acceptance/expected-schedule.json; do not invent extra alarms or weekend behavior. Model display timeline separately from alert triggers inside the same JSON so 12:00 can display ESCUELA while firing IRSE.png. Package the existing repository-root AUDIOS/ and VISUAL/ directories as Android assets using Gradle source-set configuration or an equivalent single-source approach; do not create manually maintained duplicate copies. Implement typed parsing/validation and a pure ScheduleEngine that, given Clock/ZoneId, returns current display state, next display state and next future alert. Device local wall-clock time is authoritative. Before the first weekday event and on weekends, current state is SIN_HORARIO; next may cross to the next weekday. Past alerts are always skipped and never consumed retroactively. Add focused JVM tests for all weekdays, weekend rollover, before/after boundaries, exact timestamp boundaries, malformed JSON, and missing referenced media. Keep all actual timetable values in schedule.json, not Kotlin.

items.title: Schedule resilient exact alarms
items.objective: Schedule exactly one next future AlarmClock alarm, rehydrate it after reboot/time changes, and never replay missed tasks.
acceptance: AlarmManager.setAlarmClock is used for the one next future user-visible alert; repeating alarms and WorkManager are not used for timetable firing.
The app declares the Android permissions/components required for an alarm-clock app on API 35, including USE_EXACT_ALARM and RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED.
Scheduling is recomputed after BOOT_COMPLETED, MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED, TIME_SET and TIMEZONE_CHANGED and on app activation.
Recomputation always uses ScheduleEngine and schedules only future events; elapsed/missed events are not fired and do not advance audio rotation.
PendingIntent identity is deterministic per alert occurrence and stale deliveries are rejected by occurrence id/timestamp validation.
The scheduler exposes an armed/not-armed status rather than silently claiming success when exact alarm capability is unavailable.
validation: Use a backend abstraction and JVM tests to prove next-only scheduling, cancellation/replacement, missed-event skipping and reschedule triggers.
items.taskPrompt: Implement exact scheduling using the real Android alarm-clock mechanism. The production backend must use AlarmManager.setAlarmClock with a broadcast PendingIntent to the app, and the coordinator must keep only the next future alert scheduled. The schedule engine remains the sole source for what comes next. Declare USE_EXACT_ALARM because exact alarms are core alarm-clock functionality, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, and any normal manifest requirements. Implement receivers for BOOT_COMPLETED plus sensible wall-clock/package changes (TIME_SET, TIMEZONE_CHANGED, MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED), all delegating to the same reschedule coordinator. Never catch up missed tasks after reboot or app inactivity. Protect against stale broadcasts by embedding a stable occurrence id and intended epoch timestamp and verifying it before delivery. Persist only scheduler metadata needed to cancel/validate the current occurrence; do not persist a second copy of the timetable. Add pure abstractions/fakes so JVM tests can assert which epoch would be passed to AlarmManager without relying on framework timing. Do not implement audio or full-screen UI yet.

items.title: Add full-screen alarm playback
items.objective: Turn a due alert into the intrusive lock-screen image plus one full MP3 playback, with persistent 1→2→3 rotation and automatic shutdown.
acceptance: A due alarm starts audio independently of whether the full-screen activity is actually presented, using AudioAttributes.USAGE_ALARM and the system alarm volume; the app never raises or overrides the user's alarm volume.
A high-importance CATEGORY_ALARM notification carries a fullScreenIntent and the manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT plus required foreground-service permissions for API 35.
The alarm activity uses the scheduled alert's visual asset, can show over the lock screen and turn the screen on, has no in-app dismiss/snooze control, and finishes automatically when playback ends.
Exactly one MP3 is played per delivered alert, from start to natural completion unless the OS/user externally interrupts it.
Audio choice is persistent deterministic round-robin 1.mp3→2.mp3→3.mp3→1.mp3 across process death/reboot; skipped/missed alerts do not advance it.
After playback completion or a handled playback failure, the foreground service/notification/activity are cleaned up and the coordinator schedules the next future alert.
validation: JVM tests cover round-robin persistence semantics and completion/error cleanup coordination.
Static/lint/build validation verifies the Android 15 manifest and components compile.
items.taskPrompt: Implement the real alarm experience. AlarmReceiver should hand off promptly to a foreground media-playback service that posts a high-importance CATEGORY_ALARM notification with a full-screen PendingIntent. Use the supplied MP3 assets through MediaPlayer (or another Android-native player) configured with AudioAttributes.USAGE_ALARM so playback follows the device's alarm stream. Do not programmatically change STREAM_ALARM volume and do not bypass user/system volume control. The full-screen AlarmActivity must call the supported APIs/flags to show when locked, turn the screen on, remain visible during playback, render only the scheduled image edge-to-edge, and expose no dismiss or snooze button. The service owns playback lifetime so audio still starts if Android chooses heads-up instead of launching the activity. Persist a single audio-rotation index in app private storage; advance only when a real alert successfully starts playback. On completion, stop service/notification and finish the alarm activity through an internal signal, then schedule the next future occurrence. On playback/resource failure, record/log a concrete failure, clean up, do not loop indefinitely, and continue scheduling future alerts. Use USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT and API-35 foreground-service permissions/types correctly. Keep visual/audio file names data-driven from schedule.json/audioRotation, not task-specific Kotlin branches.

items.title: Build schedule status screen
items.objective: Provide the minimal normal app screen: today's schedule, current task, next task, and only the setup actions required when alarm capabilities are missing.
acceptance: The ordinary screen displays GERMAN FATHER, today's schedule, current display state and next display state from ScheduleEngine.
There is no schedule/task editor and no hidden second source of schedule values.
Saturday/Sunday clearly show no schedule while still identifying Monday's next task when applicable.
On API 35 the app requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS when needed, checks NotificationManager.canUseFullScreenIntent(), and offers a direct system-settings action when full-screen intent access is missing.
The app checks exact-alarm capability before claiming it is armed; missing capabilities are shown as setup-required state with only the relevant setup action.
When capabilities become available on resume, the app reschedules the next future alert.
validation: Compose/view-model JVM tests verify current/next/weekend presentation from fake clocks and permission-state mapping.
Run lint/build to catch notification/full-screen API misuse.
items.taskPrompt: Implement the minimal normal UI. It is not an editor. Show the product name, today's timeline, the current task and the next task, entirely from ScheduleEngine. On weekends show SIN_HORARIO/no alarms and still compute the next weekday task. Permission/setup UI is allowed only when required to make the alarm behavior work: POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission, full-screen-intent capability via NotificationManager.canUseFullScreenIntent() with ACTION_MANAGE_APP_USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT when missing, and exact-alarm capability status. Because USE_EXACT_ALARM is declared for this alarm-clock app, do not invent a redundant custom permission flow; simply surface a failure if canScheduleExactAlarms() is false. On resume after settings changes, re-evaluate capabilities and reschedule through the existing coordinator. Keep the screen visually simple and do not add task editing, snooze, dismiss, analytics, login, network features, or cloud storage.

items.title: Add physical-device acceptance harness
items.objective: Add a debug-only path that schedules one production-pipeline alarm shortly in the future, then harden docs/tests so the real Android 15 lock-screen path can be validated.
acceptance: A debug-only exported TestAlarmHarnessActivity can be launched explicitly with delaySeconds and schedules one GIMNASIO visual alarm through the same production AlarmManager→receiver→service→notification→AlarmActivity pipeline.
The debug harness is absent from release variants and does not add any normal-screen button or production backdoor.
README documents JDK/SDK prerequisites, debug APK build/install, required Android 15 settings, how to run the debug harness, and how to inspect/retest after reboot.
The full authoritative gate and package acceptance scripts pass and app-debug.apk exists.
validation: Build debug and release-compatible variants as applicable and prove the debug component is variant-scoped.
Run all unit tests, lint, assembleDebug, schedule oracle and APK asset verifier.
items.taskPrompt: Create a physical-device acceptance seam without changing the production UX. In src/debug only, add an exported TestAlarmHarnessActivity callable explicitly by adb with an integer delaySeconds extra (default 60). It must schedule exactly one test occurrence using the existing production scheduler/delivery/playback stack and GIMNASIO.png; it must not invoke AlarmActivity directly or bypass the full-screen notification path. The harness immediately finishes after scheduling. Ensure it is not present in release/main manifests. Update README with concise Windows commands for building app-debug.apk, installing it with adb, granting/checking notification/full-screen alarm access, launching the debug harness, locking the phone before fire time, and verifying reboot rescheduling of the normal next alarm. Run/extend tests for integration contracts and keep all LAYA package files outside agent write scope. Do not add production UI controls for testing.

finalAcceptance: A debug APK builds from a clean checkout with the declared authoritative gates and can be installed on an Android 15 device.
The normal screen shows the exact schedule for the current weekday plus current and next state; it has no schedule editor.
Monday/Wednesday/Friday alerts occur at 07:00 CORRAL, 07:25 TRASTES, 08:00 PERSONAL, 08:30 GIMNASIO, 10:00 DUCHA, 10:20 TAREA, 11:20 COMER, 12:00 IRSE, 20:00 COMER, 20:40 TAREA and 23:10 DORMIR.
Tuesday/Thursday alerts occur at 07:00 CORRAL, 07:25 TRASTES, 08:00 GIMNASIO, 10:00 DUCHA, 10:20 TAREA, 11:20 COMER, 12:00 IRSE, 20:00 COMER, 20:40 TAREA and 23:10 DORMIR.
Saturday and Sunday have no alert occurrences.
At 12:00 on weekdays, IRSE is shown during the alarm while the normal timetable state is ESCUELA until 20:00.

On a locked Android 15 device with required user permissions enabled, a due alarm wakes/presents the full-screen task image and plays one MP3 through alarm audio usage; it auto-closes at natural audio completion with no in-app dismiss/snooze.
Three consecutive delivered test alarms use 1.mp3, 2.mp3 and 3.mp3 respectively, and the fourth returns to 1.mp3 even across app process death/restart.
If the phone is powered off across an alert time, that alert is not replayed after boot; the next future timetable alert is scheduled instead.
After reboot before a future alert, the app reconstructs the future alarm without requiring the UI to remain open.
Changing only schedule.json can change timetable days/times/tasks without Kotlin edits; parser/tests reject invalid references or malformed schedule data.

checks.name: Physical Android 15 full-screen alarm
checks.reason: Whether an Android 15 device wakes, presents over the actual lock screen, plays through the physical speaker at the user's alarm volume and auto-closes requires a real device and user-granted system permissions.
instructions: Use the built {artifact:debug-apk} on the target Android 15 phone.
Install/update the APK and launch GERMAN FATHER once.

Grant notification permission and, if the app reports it missing, enable full-screen alarm access in the Android system page opened by the app. Set the phone's Alarm volume to the desired high level; the app must not change it itself.
With adb available, run: adb shell am start -n com.pixatrip1984.germanfather/.debug.TestAlarmHarnessActivity --ei delaySeconds 60
Immediately lock the phone and leave the app/background untouched for at least 75 seconds.

Confirm the screen wakes/presents the GIMNASIO image over the lock screen, exactly one supplied MP3 plays, there is no in-app dismiss/snooze button, and the alarm UI/service disappears when the MP3 completes.

Repeat the debug harness three more times and confirm the audible order advances deterministically through 1.mp3, 2.mp3, 3.mp3, then 1.mp3. If the starting persisted index is not 1 because earlier tests already fired, first clear app data, relaunch, restore required permissions, and then perform this four-alarm sequence.
Send :aprobar only if all observations match; otherwise send feedback naming the mismatch.
expected: Real lock-screen presentation and audio behavior match the product contract.
Round-robin playback is persistent and deterministic.
No normal UI control can dismiss or snooze the alarm.

checks.name: Reboot restoration and missed-alert policy
checks.reason: Power-off/reboot timing and Android boot delivery on the target device cannot be faithfully established by JVM tests alone.
instructions: Choose a weekday test window where one production alert can be intentionally missed and a later production alert remains in the future; if that is impractical, use a temporary device clock adjustment only for this human test and restore automatic time afterward.
Launch GERMAN FATHER while required permissions are enabled so a future alarm is armed, then power the phone off before the chosen alert time.
Keep the phone off until after that alert time, then boot and unlock the phone.
Confirm the missed alert does not play after boot.
Keep the phone running until the next still-future scheduled alert and confirm that later alert fires normally, demonstrating boot-time reconstruction of the next future occurrence.
Send :aprobar only if the missed alert stays skipped and the later future alert is restored.
expected: No catch-up alarm is emitted for an occurrence that elapsed while the phone was off.
The next future production alarm is restored after boot.
